habitat: Forest fringes, riverine bush, bush and rock on heath-covered hillsides, and gardens. A winter visitor to eastern coastal districts.
summary: A common resident. White eyebrows, an orange upper breast, and greyish underparts. In flight it shows orange tail feathers and an orange back. The song often includes Jan-Frederik, and the alarm is a growling wur-da-wur. Avibase marks it rare, so the months are left unset. The Kemp name Cape Robin and the code NB were left unchanged.

underparts.pattern: Greyish underparts below the orange upper breast.

viewNotes.note: White eyebrows and an orange upper breast.
Orange tail feathers and an orange back.

calls.description: A continuing song, often with the phrase 'Jan-Frederik'. The alarm is a low growling 'wur-da-wur'. The grade A song is from Cape Town. The filename does not name the species.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident and a winter visitor to eastern coastal districts. Avibase marks Cape Robin-Chat rare, so the months are left unset. Greyish is not a colour name. The grade A song is from Cape Town and the filename does not name the species. The Kemp name Cape Robin and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^6=64 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 32–128.
